editorial:
You follow Hector, a regular guy spending a quiet afternoon at his country home, when a strange sight in the woods pulls him into a nightmare. After a sudden attack, he hides in a nearby lab and accidentally travels back about an hour. From there, the movie turns into a tight, stressful puzzle where every choice seems to make things worse. It feels small and grounded, but the tension keeps building as Hector tries to undo mistakes that he may have caused himself.

The acting is natural, the pacing rarely slows down, and the low-budget look actually helps the story feel real. The twists are clever without needing big effects, though some moments can feel confusing if you are not paying close attention. If you enjoy smart thrillers that reward focus, this is a great pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Hector realizes the bandaged attacker is himself from the future. To make the original timeline happen, he puts on the bandages and attacks his earlier self, forcing that version to run to the time machine. Afterward, he returns home to his wife, but the loop is already complete. The movie ends with the sense that his attempt to fix everything only locked the disaster in place.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves clever time-travel thrillers and puzzle-like stories.
